claims.text: Doxycycline is one of the initial antibiotics for an exacerbation without CF or prior cultures (with amoxicillin/clavulanate, azithromycin, clarithromycin).
claims.quote: Initial antibiotics for patients without CF and with no prior culture results should be effective against H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, S. aureus, and S. pneumoniae. Examples include amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, azithromycin, clarithromycin, and doxycycline.

claims.text: Airflow obstruction: bronchodilators (a LABA and/or a LAMA) may be used, as in COPD;
claims.quote: For patients with airway obstruction, bronchodilator therapy (eg, with some combination of a long-acting beta-adrenergic agonist [LABA] and/or a long-acting muscarinic antagonist [LAMA]) may be used as indicated by symptoms and severity of lung obstruction, similar to the use in patients with COPD

claims.text: a SABA such as albuterol relieves acute wheezing or dyspnea.
claims.quote: Short-acting beta-adrenergic agonists (SABA) such as albuterol are used to relieve acute airway obstruction causing wheezing or dyspnea.

claims.text: Influenza: treat most patients with an antiviral, typically oseltamivir, regardless of how long symptoms have lasted.
claims.quote: Most patients with bronchiectasis who develop influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infection should be treated with antiviral medications to prevent complications and development of severe disease. For influenza, treatment is typically with oseltamivir regardless of the duration of viral symptoms.

claims.text: M. avium complex: multidrug regimen with clarithromycin or azithromycin, rifampin or rifabutin, and ethambutol, until cultures are negative for 12 months.
claims.quote: Colonization with mycobacterial organisms such as M. avium complex almost always requires multiple antibiotic regimens that include clarithromycin or azithromycin; rifampin or rifabutin; and ethambutol. Antibiotic therapy is typically continued until sputum cultures, repeated every 1 to 2 months, have been negative for 12 months.
